hook: An FBI Detroit field office report documenting the November 7, 1957 interview of Wladyslaw Krasuski, a Polish ex-POW who witnessed a large circular craft rise vertically from a concealed enclosure near a German military installation at Gut Alt Golssen, approximately 30 miles east of Berlin, during 1944.
why_it_matters: This document is notable because it represents the FBI actively following up on a civilian tip prompted by a contemporaneous 1957 UFO incident in Texas — suggesting cross-referencing of current events against historical accounts. The witness is assessed on-record as showing 'no indication of mental instability,' and his account includes specific, measurable physical details (craft dimensions, cable gauges, enclosure height) and a corroborating electromagnetic effect (repeated engine stalls) consistent with other mid-century UAP reports. The wartime German military context — a concealed enclosure, SS guards, and large-gauge electrical cables — implies the craft may have been an experimental vehicle under German development.
key_findings: Krasuski described the craft as circular, 75 to 100 yards in diameter, approximately 14 feet high, with dark gray stationary top and bottom sections and a middle section rotating continuously in a blur extending the full circumference — observed from approximately 500 feet.

The craft was housed in a concealed circular enclosure approximately 50 feet high, screened by a tarpaulin, and was observed to rise vertically, clear the 50-foot wall, then move slowly horizontally until obscured by trees.

On at least two occasions — once when the noise was first heard and once during the visual observation — the tractor engine stalled and would not restart until the craft departed and the noise ceased, suggesting an electromagnetic effect on ignition systems.

Uninsulated metal cables, possibly copper, 1.5 to 2 inches in diameter, ran along or near the ground surface (in some places underwater) from a concrete column-like structure across the road to the enclosure, indicating a fixed power infrastructure associated with the craft.

The FBI Director's urgent cable to Detroit was triggered by Krasuski's letter to Robert Cutler, Special Assistant to President Eisenhower, referencing news coverage of a 1957 'rocket in Texas' causing engine stalls — the FBI explicitly linked the two incidents and ordered immediate interview.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The FBI file is classified under 'Unidentified Flying Objects, IS-X' and was generated during the same period as Project Blue Book's active investigations, with the Bureau coordinating directly with the Director's office on civilian UAP reports.

The document was screened by MARA [AF], indicating Air Force involvement in reviewing this FBI file, consistent with Wright-Patterson's role as the repository for UAP-related military records during this era.

The letter was addressed to Robert Cutler, Special Assistant to President Eisenhower, who had documented involvement in NSC-level intelligence coordination, suggesting White House-level awareness of this report.
